title: fix(short_qa): keep the SPECS line for videos without an audio stream
body:
A render without an audio stream loses the first line of `report.md`.

```python
R.append(f"SPECS ... s; audio: "
         + ", ".join(f"{s['codec_name']} ..." for s in au) if au else "NONE")
```

The conditional is attached to the whole `R.append(...)` argument, so when `au` is empty the script appends the bare string `"NONE"` instead of the SPECS line. Width, height, fps, frame count and duration then never reach the report - the numbers you need most when triaging a render that came out silent.

### Reproduce

```bash
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "testsrc2=size=1080x1920:rate=30" -t 2 -pix_fmt yuv420p silent.mp4
python templates/scripts/short_qa.py silent.mp4 out
head -1 out/report.md
```

Before:

```
NONE
```

After:

```
SPECS 1080x1920 30/1 fps, 60 frames, 2.000 s; audio: NONE
```

### Fix

Build the audio description first, then always append a complete SPECS line:

```python
au_desc = ", ".join(f"{s['codec_name']} {s['sample_rate']} Hz {s['channels']}ch" for s in au) or "NONE"
R.append(f"SPECS {v['width']}x{v['height']} {v['r_frame_rate']} fps, {v.get('nb_frames')} frames, "
         f"{float(pr['format']['duration']):.3f} s; audio: {au_desc}")
```

No duplicated f-string, 3 lines changed.

### Verification

- Silent 1080x1920 clip: line 1 is now the full SPECS line with `audio: NONE`
- The same clip with an AAC track: the complete `report.md` is **identical** to the current script's output (diffed line by line)
- Nothing else touched: black/white/frozen/pop detection, per-shot stats, contact sheets and `perframe.npz` are unchanged

title: Delete Remotion bundles after rendering to stop the temp folder filling up
body:
Hi! While using the skill I noticed the temp folder kept growing, which matches the 60+ GB issue mentioned in the Gotchas. `bridge-stills.mjs` bundles once per run but never deletes the bundle, so every stills check leaves ~1.3 GB behind.

What I changed:
- `bridge-stills.mjs` now deletes its bundle when it's done (also if a render fails), and prints a warning if old leftovers go over 5 GB
- added `clean-remotion-temp.mjs` to clean up old leftovers (dry run by default, `--yes` to delete)
- small notes in README and SKILL.md (step 11 asks the user before deleting, same as the Gotchas rule)

I tested it with a minimal Remotion project and a 300 MB `public/` folder, 3 runs each:

| Run | Before | After |
|-----|--------|-------|
| 1 | 0.33 GB | 0 GB |
| 2 | 0.65 GB | 0 GB |
| 3 | 0.98 GB | 0 GB |

Stills still render the same, and the bundle is also removed when a render fails.

Unrelated, but the Chrome path is hardcoded to `C:/Program Files/...`, which doesn't work with a per-user install. I can open another PR for that if you want.

Thanks for sharing the skill!

title: docs: use adverb in heads proportion note
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a grammar issue in `references/reports/characters.md` (line 160).

## Problem

"perfect" is an adjective modifying another adjective, "symmetric". The adverb "perfectly" is required to modify "symmetric".

The problematic text:

```markdown
They are perfect symmetric ellipses 25% too tall
```

## Fix

Replaced with:

```markdown
They are perfectly symmetric ellipses 25% too tall
```

## Summary

This PR fixes a grammar issue in `references/reports/CONTEXT.md` (line 5).

## Problem

The parenthetical repeats its own head noun ("the reference channel") and then hangs an unattached participle on it, so the clause has no verb. The intended reading is that the channel was studied privately.

The problematic text:

```markdown
next to the reference channel (the reference channel, studied
privately).
```

## Fix

Replaced with:

```markdown
next to the reference channel (studied
privately).
```

title: Add ElevenLabs narration step with automatic word timings
body:
templates/voice/eleven_voice.py generates one clip per script beat (`b01 Sentence...` lines) through the ElevenLabs with-timestamps endpoint and assembles voice.wav, words.json (word timings straight from the API, no speech-to-text pass) and beats.json (beat start/end in seconds and frames for timing the shots).

Options cover the usual revision loop: --only to redo single beats, comma-separated --voice ids to compare voices, --starts to keep redone beats on already-timed frames, --min-frames to match the composition length, --list-voices. Standard library + ffmpeg only.

The API key is read only from ELEVENLABS_API_KEY; SKILL.md tells the agent never to write it into files. SKILL.md step 3 and README updated.

title: Fix fresh installs: blank renders with current postprocessing, Windows-only script paths
body:
Fixes #14

Makes a fresh install render the bridge short on macOS/Linux with today's npm versions, without changing the look. Windows behaviour is unchanged when Chrome is installed at the old path.

## Changes
- **README:** a tested dependency set. It pins `@react-three/postprocessing@3.0.4` and explains why (3.0.5+ renders empty frames under Remotion; details in the issue), gives the three/react peer limits, and lists the 26 Kenney models (Nature Kit + Fantasy Town Kit + `Textures/colormap.png`).
- **`templates/bridge/Bridge.tsx`:** the composer children are wrapped in one fragment. 3.0.4 types children as `Element` (no `null`). A fragment creates no R3F instance, so the same passes are collected in the same order.
- **`templates/scripts/bridge-stills.mjs`:** the browser is `REMOTION_BROWSER`, else the installed Chrome on Windows (as before), else Remotion's Chrome Headless Shell. `REMOTION_TMP` now also sets `TMPDIR`. `BRIDGE_COMP` selects a renamed composition (default `BridgeShort`).
- **`templates/scripts/bridge_merge.py`:** the project root comes from the script's location (`<project>/scripts/`) instead of the placeholder.
- **SKILL.md:** one gotcha line, so the agent recognises a flat `#cfe3f2` still.

## Testing (macOS, Apple Silicon)
- `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors with the pinned set.
- Stills from these templates (frames 100 and 1200 at scale 0.5) are byte-identical (md5) to stills from my working setup. The full post chain is visible.
- `BRIDGE_COMP=NoSuchComp` fails with "Could not find composition with ID NoSuchComp", so the variable is honoured.
- `bridge_merge.py cam` run from another working directory backs up and merges into `<project>/src/videos/bridge`.
- Not tested on Windows or Linux.

title: Add optional caption-channel modules, Windows gotchas and close-up trap
body:
## What

Adds a set of **optional** modules to `SKILL.md`, all taken from a real production run: a Spanish zombie-survival short ("TORRE 12", 1080x1920, word-synced selection-box captions, SFX-only mix, ElevenLabs narration).

**Nothing in this PR changes the bridge channel's rules** (no captions, English only, music +3 dB mix, 2K export). The new sections are framed as add-on modules for channels that run captions, non-English narration, or no music.

## Why

The existing skill is proven for one channel style, but running a different channel surfaced a set of concrete, reproducible problems that the current pipeline doesn't cover:

- **ElevenLabs alignment quirk:** the API stores `"..."` ellipses as commas, so punctuation-only sentence detection silently fails. A pause-gap rule (>0.3 s between consecutive words) fixes it, verified against real word timings.
- **Hand-timed scenes drift:** deriving every scene window from the word timings (`start = words[0].ini - 0.25`, monotonic windows) means scenes re-derive automatically when timings change.
- **Word-synced captions:** a full recipe (grey→white lerp, keyword recolour, selection box on the last-spoken word only), including the hex channel-shift lerp trap that literally turned the word "zombi" blue.
- **Close-up "half a face":** facial features drawn past the head circle's edge read as the face sliding off the head. Caught on a rendered frame; fix rule + added to the Readability traps list.
- **SFX-only mix:** `adelay:all=1` + `amix normalize=0` (normalization squashes the voice under many inputs), mux with `apad`, and a `volumedetect` verification step (SFX window mean −9.5 dB vs −18 dB quiet window).
- **Thumbnail:** captions are baked into every spoken frame, so the thumbnail needs a code-constant flag (`SIN_SUBS`) — `process.env` does not reach Remotion render workers from a shell one-liner.
- **Windows/PowerShell gotchas:** the pipeline's Unix patterns (`export TEMP=...`, `cp -f`) need translation on Windows, plus the console backtick-mangling issue that breaks inline JSON edits.

## Changes

- New section `## Optional: caption-channel modules` after Pipeline step 11 (voice, scene timing, captions, close-up trap, SFX mix, thumbnail, frame-review loop)
- Pipeline steps 3 and 10 cross-reference the new modules
- 3 Windows/PowerShell entries in `## Gotchas`
- 1 entry in `## Readability traps` (close-up trap, cross-referenced)

+73 lines, −0 deletions. Docs only — no template or engine code touched, no reference material included.

title: fix(short_qa): report a freeze that runs to the last frame (#13)
body:
Fixes #13: `short_qa.py` only recorded a frozen span when a later frame
resumed motion, so a render that stalls and repeats its last frame
through the end of the export was silently dropped from the report.

The frozen-span loop now flushes a run that is still open when the
diff array ends, using the same 12-transition threshold:

```python
if run_start is not None and len(diff) - run_start >= 12:
    frozen.append((run_start, len(diff)))
```

The span end is `len(diff)`, matching the existing `(start, first-motion-frame)`
convention, so the issue's cases come out as reported:

| Input diff | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[1.0] + [0.0] * 12 + [1.0]` | `[(1, 13)]` | `[(1, 13)]` |
| `[1.0] + [0.0] * 12` | `[]` | `[(1, 13)]` |
| `[1.0] + [0.0] * 11` | `[]` | `[]` (below threshold) |

Also adds `templates/scripts/test_short_qa.py`: three stdlib-unittest
cases that build the same three synthetic videos with ffmpeg, run the
real script end to end, and read the frozen spans from `report.md`
(`python3 templates/scripts/test_short_qa.py`, 3/3 pass).

How I tested it:
- Built the three synthetic videos above and ran `short_qa.py` on each
  before the fix: the trailing-freeze video reported `[]`, the
  mid-video freeze `[(1, 13)]`, the short tail `[]` — reproducing #13.
- After the fix, the trailing-freeze video reports `[(1, 13)]` and the
  other two are unchanged.
- The new test fails on the old code (`[]` vs `[(1, 13)]`) and passes
  with the fix.
